name: Digital help for local small businesses (category)
summary: Freelance help for local shops and services with simple digital jobs: website updates, Google Business Profile listings, basic social posts and online-store setup.
whatYouDo: You meet local business owners, then update their website text and photos, set up or fix their Google Business Profile, schedule simple social-media posts, or help them start selling online. The work usually comes as small paid jobs or a monthly retainer that you arrange yourself.
appeal: Ontario's publicly funded Digital Main Street squads offered this kind of help (website creation, Google Business Profiles, social media, e-commerce), which shows the need
An Ontario government discussion paper said 40% of Ontario small businesses had no website
BDC's 2026 study found 96% of SMEs were investing in digital technology in 2025
Flexible, local, part-time work where face-to-face meetings build trust
watchOuts: Subsidies that paid for this help have shrunk: the federal CDAP stopped new advisor-grant applications in February 2024, and Brampton reported in 2025 that the future of Ontario's Digital Main Street grants was awaiting provincial updates
Where free government-funded squads still run, they offer similar help at no cost
You must find clients, set prices and chase invoices yourself; no source gave typical rates
Most businesses already have some web presence (89% in 2021, per Statistics Canada), so the work is often fixing and updating rather than building from scratch
Register for GST/HST once taxable revenue passes $30,000 in a quarter or over four consecutive quarters

compensation.notes: No reliable Canadian rate data was found for this kind of freelance work. You set your own prices.

reliability.notes: Depends on finding and keeping local clients. Retainers (monthly posting or updates) are steadier than one-off jobs.

applicationSteps: Pick two or three services you can do well, such as Google Business Profile setup, website text and photo updates, or a monthly social-post package
Practise on a friend's or community group's listing and keep before-and-after examples
Approach local businesses, your BIA or chamber of commerce, and agree scope and price in writing
Check whether a free Digital Main Street squad or local business centre already serves your area
Track income for tax and GST/HST
fitsIf: You are comfortable explaining technology to non-technical owners and want local, flexible freelance work.
notFitIf: You want a steady paycheque or dislike selling your own services.

sources.title: Published plans and annual reports 2021-2022: Ministry of Economic Development, Job Creation and Trade
sources.notes: Search-summary only. Ontario and FedDev launched the $57M Digital Main Street platform in June 2020 for up to 22,900 businesses. Squads gave one-on-one help with digital assessments, website creation, social media advertising and e-commerce. By March 2021 the program had supported 17,600+ businesses with 87 squads. The summary blended several ontario.ca pages, so the attribution to this page is likely but not certain.

sources.title: Archived - Discussion paper: shaping Ontario's small business success strategy
sources.notes: Search-summary only; archived page, date not shown. Noted that 40% of Ontario small businesses don't have a website.

sources.title: Ontario's Small Business Strategy
sources.notes: Search-summary only. Lists helping small businesses create a strong online presence under its technology pillar.

sources.title: Digital Service Squad - Support for Toronto Businesses
sources.notes: Search-summary only. Squad members give storefront businesses free one-on-one help with basic website setup, Google Business Profiles, 360° photos and social media. The Toronto program serves locally owned, independent businesses with a physical storefront.

sources.title: Survey of Digital Technology and Internet Use, 2021 (The Daily)
sources.notes: Search-summary only. In 2021, 89% of businesses had some web presence and 33% had e-commerce sales (small businesses 32%); 41% more small businesses sold online than in 2019.

sources.title: A $350B opportunity: Canada's next phase of growth to be driven by AI and digital technologies
sources.notes: Search-summary only; the summary attributed these figures to a June 2026 BDC study, and this release appears to be it. 96% of SMEs were investing in digital technologies in 2025 (91% in 2021); only 30% used AI.

sources.title: Canada Digital Adoption Program - BDC
sources.notes: Search-summary only. Businesses needed a signed CDAP grant agreement before February 19, 2024 to qualify, so the program is closed to new applicants.

sources.title: Ottawa closes key parts of $4B Canada Digital Adoption Program, leaving billions unused
sources.notes: Search-summary only (2024). The $15,000 digital-advisor grant stream closed to new applicants. At the time, the $2,400 website grants continued; their current status was not checked.

sources.title: Digital Main Street - City of Brampton
sources.notes: Search-summary only. Brampton is awaiting provincial updates on the future of the Digital Main Street Ontario Grants Program, including the Digital Transformation and Digital Service Squad grants; its own squad contract ended June 30, 2025.

sources.title: When to register for and start charging the GST/HST - Canada.ca
sources.notes: Search-summary only. GST/HST registration is required once taxable supplies exceed $30,000 in a calendar quarter or over four consecutive quarters.
